_doc: The rclone remotes the Sync tab's Rclone subpage lists. Same contract as drive-connections.json: name, type, endpoint and NOTHING that authenticates. No password, no token, no key ever appears in this file or anywhere else in data/ — the APK is a public artefact and a long-lived secret baked into it is a secret anyone can unpack (see drive-mirror-jobs.json._doc_fleet_destination for the original statement of that rule).
_doc_auth: The auth field names WHERE the fleet keeps the credential (env in the container's .secrets, oauth refresh token in the host rclone config) and what the phone itself stores (per-device bearer token behind the Android Keystore). It never contains the value.
_doc_status: status is the fleet-side truth: ok = a current host configures the remote and uses it today; unreachable = declared in the architecture spec but no current host carries the credential. A remote that is declared and unreachable MUST render its specific reason, never an empty box (#292).

remotes.name: oracle_s3
remotes.purpose: Oracle Object Storage — Google Photos Takeout archive (my-photos) and OS images (archlinux-images)
remotes.auth: OCI_S3_ACCESS_KEY + OCI_S3_SECRET_KEY env in the photoprism rclone sidecar container (.secrets)
remotes.notes: The only rclone remote a current host configures today. The photoprism sidecar mounts oracle_s3:my-photos at /opt/containers/photoprism/originals (see drive-rclone-jobs.json).

remotes.name: gdrive
remotes.auth: oauth2 refresh token in the rclone config of the retired oci-p-flex_1 host; not carried on any current host
remotes.reason: No current host configures this remote: the credential lived on the retired oci-p-flex_1 VM, and none of gcp-proxy / oci-apps / oci-analytics / oci-mail carries the refresh token.
remotes.notes: Documented in Cloud-spec.md against the former oci-p-flex_1 VM.
